problem: Find the first four non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).$

feedback.problem:
Find the first three non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).$

$\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)=$
{{field-1}}
$-\,\frac{9{x}^{3}}{2}+⋯$
feedback.worked_solution:
The Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) & =x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3!}+\frac{{x}^{5}}{5!}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Replacing $x$ with $3x$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) & =(3x)-\frac{(3x)^{3}}{3!}+\frac{(3x)^{5}}{5!}-⋯ \\  & =3x-\frac{27{x}^{3}}{6}+\frac{243{x}^{5}}{120}-⋯ \\  & =3x-\frac{9{x}^{3}}{2}+\frac{81{x}^{5}}{40}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

The Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{4!}-⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{24}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the expansions for $\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(x),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & =(3x-\frac{9{x}^{3}}{2}+\frac{81{x}^{5}}{40}-⋯)+(1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{24}+⋯) \\  & =1+3x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{9{x}^{3}}{2}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$
